name: Permanent Residency

requirements.blocker_text: Retiree route requires the applicant to be at least 62 years old.
Must own qualifying property valued at a minimum of US$350,000, maintained for at least 7 years.
requirements.fix_path: Purchase and hold qualifying property for at least 7 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires evidence of lawful residence in the Federation for at least 3 years.

evidence_required.document: Proof of property ownership (retiree route) or lawful residence history (under-62 route)
10-year clean criminal record check across countries of residence

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: minimum physical presence must be maintained per immigration rules (exact threshold not specified on source)

sources.title: Nevis Style Realty -- How to Become a Resident of St. Kitts and Nevis: two routes (retiree age 62+ with US$350k qualifying property held 7 years; under-62 with 3 years' evidenced lawful residence), EC$200 application fee plus EC$3,800 approval fee, Permanent Residency does not automatically carry employment rights (distinguishing it from Annual Residency)

Osher Advisors -- St Kitts and Nevis Permanent Residency: confirms investment-based (real estate/local business/government-approved development) and marriage-based (spouse of a citizen) pathways exist, 10-year clean criminal record check across countries of residence, financial self-sufficiency, health exam, legal entry/stay; rights include indefinite live/work, healthcare/education access, property ownership; obligations include tax compliance and minimum physical presence maintenance -- no specific residence-duration figure given for either pathway

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Saint Kitts and Nevis' initial build. STATUS: DRAFT -- both sources are tier-3 (a real estate agency and a law firm blog); no gov.kn immigration page confirming these figures was located, unlike the citizenship pathways covered by mofa.gov.kn. Two sources gave PARTIALLY CONFLICTING pictures of PR structure: nevisstylerealty.com describes two duration-based routes (retiree/under-62) with no work rights by default, while osheradvisors.com describes investment-based and marriage-based routes with full work rights implied and no duration figure -- both are plausible descriptions of overlapping but not identical PR categories (Saint Kitts and Nevis appears to route long-term non-citizen residence through several distinct administrative categories that may not be fully disambiguated by either source). work_rights modelled as 'none' per the more specific and internally detailed nevisstylerealty.com source, which explicitly states PR 'does not automatically carry employment rights' -- flagged as a potential inaccuracy for the investment/marriage sub-routes described by the other source. citizenship_after_months (168) reflects the 14-year Citizenship by Residence figure as the nearest confirmed naturalisation pathway, not a confirmed PR-to-citizenship fast-track.
